assigned.title: The automated half of the Windows matrix, running on Windows
assigned.acceptance: Every row PW-0601 marks automated runs on a windows-latest runner and fails the build when it fails. REQUIRED: the existing e2e suite runs against the DESKTOP target on Windows, not only the web target on Ubuntu -- the desktop axis is currently built on Ubuntu only, and only incidentally, because the axis defaults on and openssl happens to be installed. REQUIRED: the shell is driven end to end where the harness can reach it, and where it cannot, the row stays in the commander-machine half rather than being replaced by a unit test that proves something easier. REQUIRED: retries stay at zero, on the rule playwright.config.ts already states at length. REQUIRED: a row that is skipped says why, by name, the way the existing harness already does for the desktop and media-rig axes.
assigned.notes: PROPOSED FOR gpt-architect RULING, round 80. Created unowned as part of the WINDOWS PRODUCT COMPLETION phase board so the proposal is machine-readable rather than prose, and NOT claimed before the verdict. SURFACE NOTE: this task's allowedPaths name directories that do not exist yet. The evidence-based narrowing procedure applies to reconciling work already in history; for genuinely new work the surface is the smallest set of paths the acceptance can be satisfied within, and it is narrowed again from the diff before review if it turns out to be wider than what was written. OWNERSHIP RESOLVED BY RESPONSIBILITY in round 87, on gpt-architect's ruling. .github/workflows/windows.yml moved from allowedPaths to reviewDependencies: this task is the certification CONSUMER -- it needs the workflow and the artifact to EXIST and to execute its rows, which is a read relationship. PW-0501 owns the workflow because PW-0501 produces the Windows artifact. A task does not co-own a production build workflow merely because its tests run there. If this task's acceptance genuinely requires editing that workflow after PW-0501 lands, it is sequenced AFTER PW-0501 -- its dependencies already say so -- and its narrowed write surface is derived from the actual change at claim time rather than reserved now. Neither task was narrowed to defeat conflictWithActive; the surfaces follow the implementation responsibility. ROUND 107 AMENDMENT, on gpt-architect's ruling: .github/workflows/windows.yml has MOVED from reviewDependencies to allowedPaths -- allowedPaths is always part of the reviewed surface, so leaving it in both is redundant and ai:validate says so. This is the condition the round-87 note above named -- PW-0501 has landed, and the acceptance clause 'runs on a windows-latest runner and fails the build when it fails' cannot be satisfied without writing the only file that defines one. The surface was derived at claim time from the actual change, as that note required, and is the single file rather than .github/workflows/**. scripts/windows/** was deliberately NOT taken; it remains PW-0502's and PW-0503's. Conflict check and the cost to those two tasks' future fingerprints are recorded in the task.definition_changed event of this round.

typecheck.evidence:
The workflow is machine-checked rather than eyeballed, by the method rounds 107-109 established for this file. Every `run:` block with `shell: pwsh` is extracted from the YAML by a parser -- 7 blocks across both jobs, 2 of them new -- with ${{ runner.temp }} substituted as GitHub would substitute it, and each is parse-checked with [System.Management.Automation.Language.Parser]::ParseFile under PowerShell 7.4.6: 0 files with parse errors. The YAML itself round-trips through a parser and reports jobs [package, e2e-desktop] with the eleven named steps in order.

node --test e2e/windows/assert-desktop-axis-ran.test.mjs: 10 tests, 10 pass, 0 fail. npm run repo:validate passes and npm run ai:validate reports the board valid.

TWO DEFECTS WERE FOUND BY EXECUTING THE POWERSHELL RATHER THAN READING IT, and both are fixed. With $env:ProgramFiles unset, Join-Path threw "Cannot bind argument to parameter 'Path' because it is null"; with it defaulted, Join-Path threw "A drive with the name 'C' does not exist" -- because Join-Path is a provider-aware cmdlet that resolves the drive. Either one replaces this step's explanatory failure with an opaque one. The step now uses string interpolation and Test-Path -LiteralPath -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue, and executing both branches now produces, on the missing-openssl path, exactly the message written for an operator, naming the path searched and ending "Do NOT relax the https-only origin check in the desktop forwarder to work around it."

e2e.evidence:
WHAT IS PROVEN AND WHAT IS UNVERIFIED, SEPARATED, because this round added a Windows CI job that no Windows machine in this session can run.

PROVEN, ON REAL DATA RATHER THAN A FIXTURE. The guard that stops this job passing by skipping was run against REAL Playwright JSON reports produced here. (1) Against a report from `npx playwright test --project=api` in development mode with the desktop axis on, it read the nested suite tree correctly and reported "playback-session.desktop.api.spec.ts ran 9 case(s)" and "playback-session.cross-target.api.spec.ts ran 16 case(s)", exit 0 -- so its assumptions about Playwright's report shape hold against the real thing. (2) THE DECISIVE ONE: the same suite re-run with LIBERTY_E2E_DESKTOP=off produced a report in which all 25 desktop cases skipped; PLAYWRIGHT EXITED 0, which is exactly the silent failure PW-0602 exists to stop, and the guard exited 1 naming "0 ran, 9 skipped" and "0 ran, 16 skipped". That is the gate being seen to fail on the real failure mode, not on a hand-built record.

A THIRD DEFECT WAS FOUND THE SAME WAY AND FIXED. Run against a report from a narrowed invocation, the guard blamed openssl for a file the command had simply not selected -- a confident wrong answer that would send somebody to install a dependency they already have. It now distinguishes a file that RAN AND SKIPPED EVERY CASE (openssl, the certificate, the axis switched off) from one that CONTRIBUTED NO CASES AT ALL (never selected: a project filter, a --grep, a rename), and says both when both happened. Two further test cases cover it.

The annotation publisher was executed against the same real report and emits "::notice title=windows desktop e2e::expected=55 unexpected=0 flaky=0 skipped=8 duration=14.4s" plus the axis line; with the report absent it emits the warning branch instead and exits 0.

UNVERIFIED, AND NOT CLAIMED. The `e2e-desktop` job has NEVER RUN. No Windows runner has executed it, this session cannot push, and nothing here establishes that `npm ci` in e2e, `npx playwright install chromium`, the two Next servers, the loopback stub or the suite itself behave on windows-latest as they do on Ubuntu. What is established is that the YAML parses, every PowerShell block parses, the two blocks that could be executed here were executed on both their branches, and the guard works on real reports. The first real run is the evidence for everything else, and this gate must not be read as that evidence.

A SECOND LIMIT, STATED IN THE WORKFLOW ITSELF: the job runs in DEVELOPMENT mode only. GitHub service containers are Linux-only, so the production-with-a-database rung cannot be reached on windows-latest without installing and administering PostgreSQL on the runner. That rung stays on Ubuntu and is claimed by nothing here.

assigned.title: No test drives a signed-in viewer through to an operable player on a production build
assigned.acceptance:
THE GAP, ESTABLISHED BY READING THE SUITE RATHER THAN BY IMPRESSION. `establishSession` in e2e/src/identity.ts performs a real sign-up and sign-in against a production build, and it is imported by exactly four specs: playback-session.api, playback-session.cross-target.api, playback-session.desktop.api and rights-boundary.api. Every one of them is an API spec. NO BROWSER SPEC IN THIS SUITE EVER SIGNS IN FOR REAL. The browser specs that touch a player -- player-controls.spec.ts and keyboard-reachability.spec.ts -- skip on a production build because a deployment with no catalog source serves a refusal, and round 108 found that PW-0306's own e2e had only ever run in development, where /watch answers without an identity at all.

So the product's central journey is proven in two halves that never meet: the API knows an authenticated session can obtain a playback session, and the browser knows a player can be operated by someone who never signed in. Nothing joins them, and the join is where a rights or session regression would actually land.

REQUIRED: one spec that walks the whole journey on a PRODUCTION build -- sign in as a real account, reach an authorized title, obtain a session through the ordinary route, land on the player, and operate a control -- with each step asserted rather than assumed.
REQUIRED: the fail-closed half, in the same spec. An unauthenticated viewer and a viewer without rights to the title are both REFUSED, and the refusal is asserted as a refusal rather than as the absence of a player.
REQUIRED: the catalog question is answered honestly. A production build with no catalog source serves a refusal, so this spec either provisions a catalog source the production build will accept, or it states precisely which rung of the journey it therefore cannot reach. A SKIP WITH A REASON IS AN ACCEPTABLE ANSWER AND A SILENT PASS IS NOT.
REQUIRED: non-vacuity. The spec fails if it reaches the end having asserted nothing, which is how a journey test quietly stops being one.

MUST NOT: disable authentication, relax rights enforcement, set CONTENT_RIGHTS_ENFORCEMENT to anything but strict, reach around the application into its database, or construct a /watch address the rights gate did not return. The whole value of this task is that the machinery is the real machinery; a journey that passes because a control was switched off proves the opposite of what it claims.
MUST NOT: become a second home for assertions that belong in the specs that already own them. This is the JOIN, not a rewrite of the suite.
assigned.notes:
FILED IN ROUND 109 at gpt-architect's instruction, which asked for a narrowly-scoped task 'if the board confirms that gap' and said not to fake it by disabling authentication or rights checks. The board confirms it: PL-0701 (DONE) built the harness, PL-0704/PL-0706 (DONE) were correctives on the watch route, PW-0403 (DONE) built production authentication and session resolution, and PW-0306 (DONE) made the player operable -- each one true of its own layer, none of them joining the layers on a production build.

Conflict-checked in both fields in both directions at filing. The single allowed path is a file that does not yet exist, so it collides with nothing; the existing specs it must be read against are listed as review dependencies and are deliberately NOT reserved. PW-0307 (REVIEW) names e2e/tests/series-navigation.spec.ts and PW-0310 (IN_PROGRESS) names e2e/tests/keyboard-reachability.spec.ts; neither names this file.

P0 because it is the product's central promise and because the two existing halves have ALREADY hidden one real breach between them -- PL-0703 was opened for a production rights-invariant breach in the watch route and had to be re-run as PL-0706.

typecheck.evidence: npx tsc --noEmit in e2e/: exit 0, no output. The task's single allowedPath is e2e/tests/production-playback-journey.spec.ts and it is the only file this task wrote; no application code was touched, which is deliberate -- a journey test that had to change the product to pass would not be a journey test.

e2e.evidence:
npx playwright test --project=api --project=chromium, the WHOLE suite in both configurations. PRODUCTION (LIBERTY_E2E_PORT=3177, LIBERTY_E2E_DATABASE_URL=postgres://postgres@127.0.0.1:5433/lib_wl, a real build and a real PostgreSQL): 91 passed, 51 skipped, 0 failed, 1.4m. DEVELOPMENT: 118 passed, 24 skipped, 0 failed, 2.5m. The new spec contributes 7 tests: all 7 pass in production and all 7 skip in development, with DATABASE_SESSION_SKIP_REASON's own sentence -- a development build resolves identity from headers and has no sign-in to perform.

WHAT THE SEVEN ACTUALLY ESTABLISHED, measured by probing the running production server before any assertion was written rather than by assuming. (1) An unauthenticated viewer at /watch/<id> is refused with "Sign in to watch this", is offered the way in, and gets no player-controls element. (2) THE JOIN: the same route, with a session established through the real sign-up and sign-in routes and carried into the browser, no longer asks for an account and instead reaches "Playback isn't available on this deployment", and the shell names the account. (3) The refusal names its reason -- "no authorized media provider is configured" -- and says it is a configuration gap rather than a problem with the title, which is product invariant 4. (4) The API agrees: 503, outcome unavailable, reasons containing provider_not_configured. (5) A signed-in viewer with no profile is sent to the picker.

THE JOIN TEST WAS SEEN TO FAIL. Verified by mutation: with `page.setExtraHTTPHeaders(headers)` removed so the established session is not carried into the browser, test 2 fails on the message written for it -- "a signed-in viewer was still asked to sign in, so the session established through the API did not carry into the browser" -- while test 1 keeps passing. The file was restored from a byte copy.

A FINDING WORTH THE REVIEWER'S ATTENTION: the playback API answers the SAME 503 provider_not_configured to an anonymous caller and to an authenticated one, because the provider check precedes the identity check. That is fail-closed and leaks nothing, so it is not reported as a defect -- but it means the API alone cannot demonstrate that authentication did anything on this deployment. The browser can, and that is why the evidence above rests on the CHANGE OF REFUSAL rather than on a status code.

WHAT IS NOT PROVEN, AND WHY IT IS AN EXTERNAL BLOCKER RATHER THAN A GAP HERE. The journey does not reach an operable player. A production build refuses the demo catalog on purpose -- presenting invented titles from a hosted build would present them to a reader as the product's catalog -- and the only licensed source is a live CC0 query, a network dependency a gate should not have. And no authorized media provider is configured: PL-0302 owns that and is BLOCKED on "a confirmed licensed API/provider and credentials", which is a purchase and an authorization rather than an engineering step. Two of the seven tests PIN that boundary and FAIL ON SUCCESS, telling whoever configures a provider or a catalog to extend the journey rather than to update the expectation.

NOTHING WAS DISABLED TO REACH THIS. CONTENT_RIGHTS_ENFORCEMENT stayed strict, the identity system is the real one, the session is a real row in PostgreSQL, no address was constructed that the rights gate did not return, and no application file was changed.

recommended.title: Install, upgrade, uninstall, reinstall — tested, not assumed
recommended.acceptance: The installer's lifecycle is exercised automatically wherever that is possible on a runner, and everything that is not is named for the commander's machine. REQUIRED: clean install on a machine that has never had the application, then launch. REQUIRED: upgrade over a previous version with user data preserved, which is the one a release breaks most often and nobody tests. REQUIRED: uninstall leaves no service, no scheduled task and no orphaned node.exe, and states exactly what user data it keeps or removes. REQUIRED: reinstall after uninstall. REQUIRED: each case is marked automated or commander-machine, with the reason, so the split is visible rather than implied.

review.evidence: CHANGES REQUESTED at 835823561c69f5bbdebf19c637eeeabff19dacf7. Transcribed by claude-lead from gpt-architect's round-105 ruling, section 2, which is a request for changes in substance even though it does not use the word: 'The lifecycle harness architecture is accepted. DO NOT mark PW-0503 DONE merely to free the Test lane. Current Windows evidence establishes only part of the lifecycle matrix.' gpt's itemised verdict: F1 clean install PARTIAL PASS -- the MSI builds, installs and its installed tree is verified; still unverified is actual installed application launch and WebView runtime. F2 upgrade UNVERIFIED -- no real previous release has been exercised as an upgrade source, so user-data preservation across an actual upgrade remains unproven. F3 uninstall PARTIAL PASS -- msiexec uninstall executes; still to prove where automation permits are no orphaned service, no scheduled task, no orphaned node.exe, expected files removed, and documented user-data retention behaviour. F4 reinstall UNVERIFIED but AUTOMATABLE -- 'implement and execute this rather than classifying it as commander-only'. WHAT HAS CHANGED SINCE THAT VERDICT WAS WRITTEN, and it narrows the request rather than answering it: the IMPLEMENTATION of F3's residue classification and of F4 reinstall already exists in scripts/windows/lifecycle.mjs and residue.mjs at the commit above, with 30 cases behind the decisions, and F4 is already marked plannedAutomated with no manual portion. What does not exist is EXECUTION, and it cannot be created by any open task: no open task can write .github/workflows/windows.yml -- every writer is DONE and PW-0502, PW-0503 and PW-0602 hold it read-only. That is recorded as a board.sequencing_finding and needs a ruling on which task gets the write surface. Recorded so the task leaves REVIEW honestly rather than being completed on evidence gpt declined to accept.
